why: Keeps the page number 247 continuing the preceding page's numbered running head; otherwise the two are wording variants.
Continues the preceding page's practice of translating the element names rather than transliterating them, and does not insert an unevidenced chapter heading in the middle of a numbered verse run.
Preserves the 1902 register of the preceding page (peculiar to it, function of phase, moments of momentum) and the mid-sentence opening, where the other modernizes and inserts a doubled gloss.
Keeps the Arabic-script convention the preceding page uses for variant readings, and retains the grammatical commentary the other drops in racing on to the next verse.

Completes the sentence cut at 'laid up' without interposing a running header, and its Greek-variant note ('In a strong city') matches the verse text it annotates, where the other's note contradicts its own rendering.
Both complete the dangling clause about Tiberius; one carries the running head, the other the ellipsis, and the wording differences are of equal quality.
Keeps the preceding page's italic-emphasis markup and the page/section numbering, both of which the other drops.
The other leaks an editorial artifact, '[Modernized from p. 43]', into the body; this one opens with the book's running header.
Keeps the footnote markers and the footnote block at the foot of the page, which the other drops entirely.
Identical but for comma placement.
Completes 'apprehended / as absolutely good' exactly, where the other redundantly restates the verb ('considered as'), and keeps the preceding page's heavy italicization of key terms.
Completes the sentence left hanging on 'walked unseen through the palace and' with 'escaped'; the other drops that word and starts a new sentence.
Keeps the preceding page's italicized Japanese terms (o-mon) where the other drops one and leaves a broken inline gloss, 'palanquins sedan chairs carried by bearers'.
Capitalization and comma variants of the same Seneca rendering.
The other inserts '[...continued from previous page]', an editorial artifact absent from the source, and drops the heading markup; this one continues the legal sentence directly.
Keeps the preceding page's italics for titles and terms (Zohar, Bahir), which the other drops.
Both complete 'to propitiate the goddess / and to avert epidemics' identically; the rest is comma variance.
Keeps Hrimthurs untranslated in the body as the preceding page does, and the archaic register; the other switches to 'Frost Giants' and modernizes.
One normalizes the long s and keeps the page number, the other renders Agrippa's 'not from them but through them' more clumsily; neither dominates at the junction.
The other carries a broken inline gloss ('the Ghostly Power Ghostly Power: Spiritual/divine power...') and a garbled double negative.
Keeps the preceding page's parenthetical-gloss convention (somnambulism (sleepwalking)...), which the other drops entirely, plus the page number and the correct singular verb after 'series'.
The other garbles the subject — 'Genji watched a servant helping him into his cloak' — where this one keeps the pronoun reference coherent and carries the running head.
Keeps 'in Rome' consistently as established earlier in the same passage; the other switches to 'at Rome' at the end.
Completes 'the male's penis to enter / the internal cavity of the uterus' directly, where the other redundantly restates the verb ('and for it to enter').
Keeps the Latin citation title asse italicized as the preceding page keeps its Latin titles; the other translates it as 'the total estate'.
One reads cum civibus better, the other the Erythraean line; the verse layout and italics are the same.
The other breaks the heading with a stray '##' and inverts 'how few are there who do not think' into 'how many', reversing the sense.
Keeps the 'first... secondly' parallel and the active construction; the other garbles the first clause ('commit sin here, but instead do so out of').
Uses one abbreviation for the chorus throughout (Chor.), where the other alternates between Cho. and Chor. on the same page.
Renders castellum Emmaus as the village of Emmaus where the other gives 'the castle of Emmaus', and keeps plural agreement across the list of miracles.
Continues the preceding page's English common plant names (Heather, Chaste Tree, Radish, Date Palm); the other switches to Latin forms (Erica, Agnus, Raphanus, Phoenix).
Picks up the carried subject 'the blossoming youth' with an attaching participle and a finite verb; the other's 'granted through remedies' attaches to nothing.
Keeps the 'concerning X' parallel through the topic lists and the capitalized Church; the other switches to 'of X' mid-list.

Names Sapor, which the following parenthesis ('corruptly called King Sabor') needs in order to mean anything, and reads 'that one of Phoebus / the orator' as a phrase rather than capitalizing it into a name.
The other leaves a sentence fragment ('for he who seeks the peace of the Churches through you, if controversies are first rightly judged').
Continues the preceding page's 'Whether X' question form exactly; the other switches the whole list to 'Does X?' interrogatives.
Renders Antonius's 'not for utility but for pleasure' as one clean antithesis where the other breaks it into a comma splice, and keeps the 'just as... so' comparison intact.
Continues the carried 'with this body, with this soul, with / with our whole organ' parallel, which the other breaks into 'in our entire body', and keeps the page's polysyndeton.
Attaches to the cut phrase 'according to the...' with a noun phrase; the other opens on a dangling participle ('breathing the spirit of our own') that completes nothing.
Each keeps one of the preceding page's conventions and breaks the other — quoted titles against translated rather than transliterated terms.

Keeps the preceding page's transliterated title convention (Chu Ci) and a consistent 'X Customs' heading pattern; the other translates the title and alternates between 'Degenerate Customs' and 'Customs of Ignorance'.
Near-synonymous renderings of the same narrative; no continuity signal either way.
The preceding page cites Lunheng romanized, and this one keeps Han Shu / Hou Hanshu / Tang Shu in the same form where the other translates them; it also has the correct Yonghui era.
'Every perfection must be submitted to' keeps the preceding page's khushu'/submission sense, where the other introduces 'revered'.
Renders the verse consistently in English; the other leaves 'siwa tanzin' untranslated and meaningless in the middle of a line.
The preceding page renders the tawakkul root as 'rely' without exception and this one keeps that; the other mixes 'rely' and 'trust' within the same chain of verses.
Keeps the Arabic grammatical examples transliterated, which the other translates away and so destroys the grammatical point, and marks the technical terms consistently.
Near-synonymous renderings of the Typhon description; no consistent continuity signal either way.
Keeps the preceding page's key terms 'gathering' and 'servant' running through the passage; the other replaces them with 'acquired'/'wheat' and 'worker'/'merchant'.
Keeps the KJV phrasing ('prepared the temple', 'So all the service of the Lord was established') and leaves the stray catchword 'after' between sentences, where the other embeds it mid-verse.
The preceding page is wholly in English, and this one translates the section heading where the other leaves it in German ('Endzweck und Nutzen der Einsicht').
Supplies 'that I should make room for him', completing the clause the previous page left hanging on 'demanded', which the other leaves without its subject.
The preceding page is wholly in English, and this one translates the running head ('HISTORY OF YUCATAN') where the other leaves it in Spanish.
Completes the carried clause properly and keeps the page in English as the preceding page is; the other reverts the proper nouns to Dutch (Portugysen, Indien, Catholijke Religie).
Ties Monacensis to Munich and the Bavarian State Library as the preceding page's 'collated in Munich' requires, keeps the period name Breslau, and bolds the names consistently.

Its opening line picks up the preceding stanza's 'not even one was obtained', where the other opens on an unconnected line, and it keeps the royal title Yang Dipertuan as the page keeps its other Malay terms.
